terms.grammar: adjective, comparative of superus; genitive superiōris
evidence: Cic. Att. 12.10: tōta domus superior vacat (Lewis & Short)
Caes. B.G. 7.46: superiōrem partem collis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The upper of two, or the higher part of a thing: labrum superius, the upper lip; in superiōre parte, upstream (Plin. Ep. 8.8.6). Also earlier, former (superiōre annō), and stronger, victorious (Lewis & Short). The i is a vowel.

evidence: Plaut. Merc. 5.1.1: līmen superum inferumque (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The positive, rarer in this plain sense: līmen superum, the lintel; superī, the gods above, and the living. The superlative summus is the top of a thing (see surface).

phrases.latin: ad rīvum eundem lupus et agnus vēnerant sitī compulsī; superior stābat lupus longēque īnferior agnus
phrases.english: a wolf and a lamb had come to the same stream, driven by thirst; the wolf stood higher up, and the lamb far below

phrases.latin: in superiōre parte nāvigāre tantum, īnfrā etiam natāre concessum
phrases.english: in the upper part only boating is allowed; lower down you may swim as well
the whole upper part of the house is empty

sources: Lewis & Short: superus · Lewis & Short: superior
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 58.
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-phaedrus, loci-plinius), checked against the editions named there. Cicero, Caesar and Plautus as Lewis & Short quotes them (s.v. superus).
